paper.title: Contextual Safety Reasoning and Grounding for Open-World Robots
paper.central_claim: CORE lets a robot infer context-dependent safety constraints online from visual observations with a VLM, ground them into spatial safe sets and enforce them with control barrier functions, with probabilistic safety guarantees under perception uncertainty, without prior maps or safety specifications; it rivals an oracle with ground-truth context and clearly outperforms prior semantic-safety style methods that lack online contextual reasoning.
paper.central_claim_source: son55 wording (English); sol wording retained in input seat file.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: EVIDENCE.md transfer clause "sim-to-real with real trial counts" is met mechanically (Spot, 6 tasks x 5). Weakest reading: the method is training-free, the 100-image development set is "sampled from our experimental setup" (whether it includes the hardware lab is unstated), the Spot depth pipeline was engineered for hardware, and hardware success judging is not described.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 12 authored simulated tasks and 6 lab tasks, a VLM-predicate + segmentation + CBF filter prevents most contextually unsafe nominal plans (sim 28/30 unsafe prevented vs 5/30 for an LLM-written-rules proxy under the same CBF; hardware 26/30 vs geometric 15/30) while rarely blocking safe ones; the 90% certificate holds only under a same-setup calibration, an acknowledged non-conservative independence assumption and a latency below the measured one.
not_supported: outperforming actual prior semantic-safety methods (only an authored No Context proxy)
importance of spatial grounding (no grounding ablation despite the abstract)
open-world generalization beyond the prompt's five categories
assessment.retained_improver_online_transfer: retained/improver: not applicable (static safety layer); online: yes; transfer: sim-to-real with counts (weakest reading).

scope_ruling.reason: Unlike 2606.12372 (no LLM/VLM in any role; human teacher; learned intervention module), CORE wraps a frozen general-purpose VLM with perception tools (SAM3, depth projection) and an execution-control layer (CBF-QP) in the closed control loop of a mobile/legged robot; EVIDENCE.md lists verification/monitoring and execution control as harness components and admits safety research for such systems. The absence of an LLM agent loop that chooses actions makes it borderline: the VLM gates the controller rather than planning. Scored as in scope; controller may reverse (all rating evidence would remain valid).

G.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Concrete limitation (rules supplied a priori by a user/expert) with neighbour families named; the No Context and Geometric failures under the same CBF give in-paper evidence for the residue; cited prior systems are not run.

M.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Predicate representation, grounding operators, SDF barrier and QP are reconstructable and aimed at the gap; the certificate's modelling (average Bernoulli detection, gamma=0 flagged non-conservative) is thin.

X.reason: Resolved for sol (2) over son55 (3). The static pipeline is fully specified (operators, full prompt, thresholds, alpha, camera intrinsics, latencies), but the third claimed contribution - enforcement with a probabilistic guarantee - is executed with internal inconsistencies: gamma = 1/3 of risk in Sec V-E vs gamma = 0 in App. B-D3; certificate latency ~3 s vs measured 4.37 s + 0.75 s; measurements within 3 m discarded although safe initialization requires hazards be detected before entry. Anchor 2 (main steps described, key conditions unclear/contradictory).

measurement.reason: Resolved for sol (2) over son55 (3). Closed-loop outcomes are counted (60 sim, 30 hardware) with module-level failure attribution, but: ground truth for the 100-image predicate set (which drives VLM choice and the calibration) is undescribed; the hardware success judge is undescribed; hardware attribution percentages (3.9%, 9.0%) are not attainable with 30 trials (SE1); and the "empirical validation" of a distribution-level certificate is a comparison with a 28/30 task count. Anchor 2 (verifier/denominator gaps).

causality.reason: Resolved for sol (3) over son55 (2). The central gain (online visual context) is isolated with model prompt logic, grounding and CBF held fixed (No Context: LLM writes rules pre-deployment with the same system prompt), Oracle bounds it from above, and module-level failure attribution shows the mechanism (context errors 43.3% vs 3.3%). Missing pieces (grounding/CBF ablations; real prior systems; hardware only vs Geometric) bear on secondary claims, which are marked not_supported rather than lowering the central attribution to the anchor-2 "unseparated confound" level.

holdout.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Hardware lab and Spot are a new setting, but VLM choice, prompt ablations and certificate calibration use 100 images from the evaluation setup, and scenario families are authored by the paper.

statistics.reason: Resolved for sol (2) over son55 (1). Five randomized-start repeats per task with stated denominators and failures decomposed by module in sim and hardware; no intervals, variance or paired tests, and the hardware attribution does not reconcile with its denominator. Anchor 1-2 ("counts but no variance, failures not decomposed") - failures are decomposed, so 2.

cost.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Per-module latency, memory for every VLM and the accuracy/latency trade-off are reported; no token counts or baseline compute comparison; certificate latency differs from measured.

status_reason: Complete fixed text with Appendices A-B and full prompt read; all eight items resolved.
initial_evidence_judgment: Read in full before seat rating reasons. A frozen 4-bit Gemma 3 27B VLM, prompted with a structured safety logic, emits JSON predicates (ON/NEAR/AROUND/BETWEEN over semantic classes) from RGB; SAM3 segments the classes, depth back-projects them into a count grid, a thresholded safe set becomes a signed-distance barrier, and a CBF-QP minimally modifies a nominal waypoint/PID controller. A Ville-inequality argument gives a trajectory-level certificate conditioned on a calibrated detection function. Sim (Isaac, 3 environments x 4 tasks x 5): CORE 57/60 vs Oracle 59/60, No Context (LLM writes rules before deployment, same CBF) 33/60 with 5/30 unsafe prevented, Geometric 30/60 (0/30 unsafe). Spot hardware (6 tasks x 5): 26/30 vs geometric 15/30. Predicate accuracy on 100 images from the experimental setup drives VLM choice, prompt ablations and certificate calibration. Problems found: hardware failure attribution 3.9% and 9.0% are not multiples of 1/30 and do not sum to the 13.3% failure rate; certificate uses ~3 s latency while Table A.I reports 4.37 s reasoning + 0.75 s grounding; main text assigns gamma one third of the risk while the appendix sets gamma=0 under a self-described non-conservative assumption; the abstract claims a grounding ablation that does not exist; measurements within 3 m are discarded, which interacts with the safe-initialization assumption. Scope: no LLM agent loop chooses actions, but a frozen general-purpose VLM with perception tools sits inside the control loop and gates execution (verification/execution-control layer). Initial judgment: in scope (borderline, class A component), system_method, transfer by the sim-to-real-with-counts clause (weakest reading), claim scoped: contextual filtering works on the authored scenarios; the guarantee is conditional.
